Questions-only timed practice: first session

Unit 1 · Week 16 · Lesson 1 · Suggested 55-minute plan; adjust to local timing.

Prepare: Public revision sample, not a secure assessment or grade predictor. Record prior exposure. Use questions only: no answers, examples, code execution or partner help during the independent window. If support is used, stop the independent clock and label that work supported. The two-session suggestion is 5 minutes reading plus 40 + 15 working minutes; record actual time and any interruption. For practice use unit1-practice-paper.md, unit1-practice-answers.md only after closure, and unit1-practice-record.md. For a school task use only the school-issued materials.

Suggested answers are teacher guidance, not extra assessment tasks. These notes are public.

Purpose and attempt conditions

Timed formative practice: attempt: Public revision sample, not a secure assessment or grade predictor. Record prior exposure. Use questions only: no answers, examples, code execution or partner help during the independent window. If support is used, stop the independent clock and label that work supported. The two-session suggestion is 5 minutes reading plus 40 + 15 working minutes; record actual time and any interruption.

Questions-only practice paper · Attempt, feedback and retry record

1. Questions-only timed practice

Suggested time: 2 minutes

Instructional strategy: Purpose and exposure check

This is timed formative practice, not a school-issued assessment or a grade predictor. Record actual time and exposure. The public questions/answers can be accessed beforehand, so freshness is never assumed.

2. Confirm the practice conditions

Suggested time: 3 minutes

Instructional strategy: Independent-attempt boundary

Use unit1-practice-record.md. If students have seen a question/model, record repeat practice or use a teacher-supplied changed version. No question-specific content is modelled in this deck. Support stops the independent clock for that work; do not combine supported and independent evidence.

3. Reading time: 5 minutes

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Questions-only reading

Suggested reading allowance 5 minutes. The sample has 12 questions and suggests 55 working minutes. This split plan uses 40 working minutes today and 15 at the start of Lesson 2. Teachers may select a smaller section and record its scope/timing instead; do not imply a full paper was completed.

4. Independent working time: first 20 minutes

Suggested time: 20 minutes

Instructional strategy: Timed formative attempt

Start the independent working clock. Hold this neutral slide; do not discuss paper Q3, show a trace or reveal question-specific hints. Teacher clarifications must not solve questions; record support and interruptions.

5. Independent working time: next 20 minutes

Suggested time: 20 minutes

Instructional strategy: Timed formative continuation

Continue to 40 working minutes in this session. This slide is a time cue, not a discussion break. No worked solution or compound-question model is shown before the attempt is preserved.

6. Pause and preserve the original

Suggested time: 2 minutes

Instructional strategy: Attempt preservation

Pause the clock. Preserve the unedited response and note the stopping point. Follow the teacher’s storage/collection arrangement; do not complete questions at home before the continuation. A split session is not a continuous examination.

7. Record exposure and support

Suggested time: 2 minutes

Instructional strategy: Evidence labelling

The record is a learning aid, not a score or authentication certificate. Prior-seen answers remain repeat practice even when the current window had no help. If a learner opens the key between sessions, record that exposure before continuing.

8. Next lesson: continue before feedback

Suggested time: 1 minutes

Instructional strategy: Continuation briefing

Do not run an answer discussion as an exit activity. Keep uncertain steps for the continuation and later feedback. School conditions supersede this suggested practice arrangement.
